Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas · Body, health & movement

sense noun

sight, hearing and the rest

also the five senses, sense of smell, sense of taste, sense of touch

classical

Cic. N. D. 2.140: Sēnsūs autem interpretēs ac nūntiī rērum
Cic. de Or. 3.99: gustātus, quī est sēnsus ex omnibus maximē voluptārius

sēnsus, sēnsūs m.

noun, fourth declension

a sense; feeling, perception

The five are vīsus (sight), audītus (hearing), odōrātus (smell), gustātus (taste) and tāctus (touch) (Traupman 58–59).

Examples

  • cum autem paulum firmitātis accessit, et animō ūtuntur et sēnsibus cōnītunturque, ut sēsē ērigant, et manibus ūtuntur et eōs agnōscunt, ā quibus ēducantur

    but when they have a little strength, they use their minds and their senses, try to stand up, use their hands, and know the people who are bringing them upCic. Fin. 5.42

  • Sēnsūs autem interpretēs ac nūntiī rērum in capite tamquam in arce mīrificē ad ūsūs necessāriōs et factī et conlocātī sunt.

    The senses, the interpreters and messengers of things, have been made and placed in the head, as in a citadel, wonderfully fitted for what we need.Cic. N. D. 2.140

See also feel, hear, touch, sense.
